guidelines.text: Wipe liquid spills and water puddles immediately using an absorbent cloth or dry mop.
Place non-skid rubber-backed mats at sink, bathtub, and exterior doorway transitions.
Apply anti-slip adhesive tread strips or slip-resistant treatments to polished stone and wet bathroom tiles.
Keep infants and elderly relatives away from wet or freshly mopped surfaces until thoroughly dried.
Fasten trailing electrical cables along walls or baseboards using adhesive cord clips or protective raceways.
Clear walking corridors, hallways, and stairs of footwear, cardboard boxes, and loose clutter.
Secure area rug perimeters with double-sided rug tape or transition grips to eliminate raised curled edges.
Store children's toys in low floor bins away from main walking lines immediately following play.
Disconnect and replace damaged, pinched, or frayed power cords without attempting temporary tape repairs.
Relocate power strips, chargers, and extension cords away from sinks, basins, and moisture sources.
Insert protective plastic safety caps or sliding tamper-resistant covers into all unused low wall outlets.
Avoid daisy-chaining multi-socket adapters; distribute high-draw heating or cooling appliances across separate branch circuits.
Turn cookware and pan handles inward toward the rear of the stovetop to prevent accidental snagging or tipping.
Maintain at least 1 metre (3 feet) of open clearance between portable space heaters and curtains, bedding, or upholstery.
Store matches, utility lighters, and hot appliances out of reach of children in elevated, latched locations.
Turn off heating appliances, stoves, and irons immediately when stepping away from the area.
For grease or oil cooking pan flare-ups, slide a tight metal lid over the pan and switch off heat; never pour water.
For small burning paper or textile fires, extinguish using plenty of water or a multipurpose extinguisher.
Store culinary knives, shears, and razor blades in a wall-mounted magnetic rack, knife block, or latched drawer.
Collect broken glassware fragments using a broom and dustpan, followed by a damp paper towel to pick up micro-splinters.
Push food preparation cutting boards and sharp cutlery well back from countertop perimeters away from toddler reach.
Wrap spent razor blades or sharp glass shards in rigid cardboard before placing them in the disposal bin.
Mount hardware-secured safety barrier gates at both the summit and base of interior staircases.
Engage window sash restrictors to ensure residential window openings cannot exceed 10 centimetres (4 inches).
Install continuous, solidly anchored handrails spanning the entire vertical run on both sides of stairways.
Move chairs, ottomans, and climbable furniture away from balcony perimeters and open windows.
Anchor tall bookcases, dressers, and storage wardrobes directly into wall studs using anti-tip bracket straps.
Mount flat-screen televisions securely to wall studs or secure them with anti-tip straps to broad, low media furniture.
Arrange storage weight distribution so heavy books and boxes occupy the lowest shelves to preserve stability.
Remove desirable toys, remote controls, or sweets from upper furniture tops to discourage climbing behavior.
Store domestic chemical cleaners, bleach, and detergents in elevated cabinets secured with child-resistant latches.
Retain pharmaceuticals in their original labeled child-resistant containers within a locked medicine cabinet.
Never decant chemical solvents, kerosene, or cleaning mixtures into unlabelled beverage bottles or drink containers.
Program regional poison information hotline numbers into mobile speed-dial and post conspicuously near exits.
Collect and store coins, button batteries, pins, and small objects under 3 cm well outside infant and toddler reach.
Ensure electronic gadgets and toy battery compartments are secured with screwed closures to prevent battery release.
Inspect plush and plastic toys regularly for loose eyes, detached buttons, or split seams.
Dispose of burst balloons and brittle broken plastic fragments immediately upon detection.
Empty standing water from washing buckets, plastic tubs, and utility basins immediately after finishing tasks.
Maintain uninterrupted direct visual contact with infants and toddlers whenever they are near bathtubs or water receptacles.
Fasten rigid, weight-bearing, padlocked covers over underground sumps, storage wells, and rainwater harvesting cisterns.
Keep bathroom and laundry facility doors shut and fitted with child-resistant exterior latch closures.
Install safety cleats at least 1.5 metres above the floor to wrap and secure loose window blind pull cords.
Position infant cribs, playpens, and toddler beds well away from window treatments, curtain cords, and appliance wires.
Tie plastic packaging bags into tight knots and dispose of them promptly outside child reach.
Verify that crib vertical slats and stair rail balusters have gaps no wider than 6 centimetres (2.3 inches).
Restrict access beneath areas of loose ceiling plaster, structural fractures, or unstable overhead elements.
Arrange for a qualified structural engineer or licensed contractor to assess severe masonry wall or beam cracks.
Repair pipe leakages and scrub active black mould growth using detergent solutions while wearing protective respirators.
Fasten or replace loose banisters, rotting floorboards, or detached floor threshold transition strips.
Install bright, even, glare-free illumination along stairways, dark corridors, and entry thresholds.
Plug automatic motion-activated nightlights into wall sockets along bedroom-to-bathroom nocturnal walking routes.
Replace expired bulbs immediately and ensure two-way light switches are accessible at both stair top and landing.
Apply high-contrast visual edge striping along stair tread edges to assist depth discernment in shadowed zones.
Keep residential perimeter gates and driveway barriers latched to prevent uncontrolled child access to roadways.
Level sunken paving slabs, fill potholes along walkways, and clearly mark irregular exterior steps.
Report low-hanging, damaged, or sagging exterior utility cables to local authorities without attempting contact.
Ensure children wear reflective apparel and maintain firm hand-holding with adults when walking near vehicle thoroughfares.
Isolate the observed unusual physical anomaly and restrict access by vulnerable occupants until assessed.
Inspect the item from a prudent physical distance to establish whether specialised technical evaluation is required.
Consult manufacturer specifications or local safety codes if the unfamiliar equipment or hazard cannot be readily resolved.

H01.text: Dry or clean slippery walking surfaces and proceed with caution across the area.

H02.text: Remove obstacles, clutter, and loose trailing wires from primary walking routes.

H03.text: Disconnect unshielded or damp electrical equipment and avoid contacting exposed wiring.

H04.text: Extinguish open flames, switch off unattended heat appliances, and isolate combustibles.

H05.text: Place exposed blades or glass fragments into secure containers away from reach.

H06.text: Maintain physical distance from elevated edges and install protective barriers where drops exist.

H07.text: Stabilize or anchor tall, top-heavy furniture and remove stacked items from high perches.

H08.text: Lock chemicals and pharmaceutical products in elevated storage inaccessible to children.

H09.text: Store small loose parts, coins, and button batteries in sealed, out-of-reach containers.

H10.text: Drain open standing water vessels and fit secure covers onto water cisterns.

H11.text: Wrap hanging cord loops high on wall cleats and discard thin plastic wrappers.

H12.text: Cordon off structurally damaged elements and schedule professional building repairs.

H13.text: Improve area illumination with suitable lighting fixtures to remove shadows and glare.

H14.text: Latch perimeter gates and watch for road traffic and ground depressions when walking outdoors.

H15.text: Keep individuals away from the unclassified anomaly and conduct a careful manual inspection.

universal_fallback.text: Keep people away from the hazard area, isolate or remove the hazard if feasible without risk, and consult a qualified technician if required.
